extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('expr') is passed directly to eval() function. This allows arbitrary Python code execution. Despite the attempt to restrict __builtins__, attackers can still execute dangerous code through various techniques.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: User-controlled JSON from request.body is deserialized using json.loads() without validation and directly merged into a workset dictionary via update(). This allows attackers to modify internal object properties including is_admin and credit_limit.

User-controlled data from request.body is passed directly to MongoDB find_one() query without sanitization. This allows NoSQL injection attacks where attackers can use MongoDB operators like $ne, $gt, $regex to bypass authentication or extract data.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: urllib.request.urlopen() is called with ssl._create_unverified_context() which disables SSL certificate verification. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks and the hardcoded endpoint could be replaced by an attacker-controlled URL if this pattern is reused elsewhere.

User input from request.GET.get('fragment') is rendered directly in a Jinja2 template without sanitization. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) attacks leading to remote code execution. Example payload: {{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__['os'].popen('id').read() }}

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Template Engines

extra.message: User-controlled filename from request.GET.get('name') is used to construct a file path without sanitization. This allows path traversal attacks allowing attackers to write files to arbitrary locations on the filesystem using sequences like ../../../etc/cron.d/malicious.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-controlled URL from request.GET.get('lane') is passed directly to redirect() without validation. This allows open redirect attacks where attackers can craft URLs like /ops/after/patient-lane-167/?lane=https://evil.com to phish users.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('copyline') is concatenated directly into an HTML response without escaping. This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks where attackers can inject malicious scripts via the copyline parameter.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The endpoint reflects arbitrary Origin header values back to Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials to true. This allows malicious websites to make authenticated cross-origin requests on behalf of users.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: The endpoint explicitly disables XSS protection by setting X-XSS-Protection to 0 and clears the Content-Security-Policy header. This makes the application more vulnerable to XSS attacks.
Hardcoded credentials (handle: 'north'/'south', verifier: '4812'/'5930') are present in the source code. These can be used as a backdoor to bypass authentication checks.
Sensitive data including request body and Authorization header are logged without sanitization. This can expose authentication tokens, credentials, or personal information in log files.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Sensitive configuration information including DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE environment variable and BASE_EXPORT_DIR path are exposed through the API response. This information can aid attackers in reconnaissance.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Hardcoded passwords for demo accounts (admin/adminpass, clinician1/clinicianpass, frontdesk1/frontdeskpass, patient1/patientpass) are present in seed data. These should be removed or randomized in production.
